Toyota’s Newest GR Racing Prototype Sure Looks Like the Next-Gen MR2

MR
By Marco Rossi Senior Supercar & Aerodynamics Editor • via Car and Driver Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Car and Driver Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • In the world of Pokemon, every pocket monster has several forms it can evolve through in order to reach its final powerful form.
  • So, you start with something that looks like a spicy salamander and eventually end up with what’s basically a dragon.
  • In Japan’s Super Taikyu series, Toyota appears to be racing something in the middle form of a Yaris evolving into an MR2, as spotted by CarBuzz .
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • MARCO ROSSI Senior Supercar & Aerodynamics Editor

The Benchmark for Track-Tolerant Engineering

In the high-stakes supercar arena, pure horsepower is no longer enough to claim supremacy. This dispatch from Car and Driver emphasizes how cutting-edge downforce balance, electronic limited-slip differentials, and hybrid torque-vectoring are reshaping driver engagement. Exotic marques must prove that extreme performance can harmonize with reliability, thermal endurance, and road compliance.

Big Picture: Lap times at benchmark proving grounds and early client allocations will reveal whether this performance envelope disrupts the existing supercar hierarchy.

In the world of Pokemon, every pocket monster has several forms it can evolve through in order to reach its final powerful form. So, you start with something that looks like a spicy salamander and eventually end up with what’s basically a dragon. In Japan’s Super Taikyu series, Toyota appears to be racing something in the middle form of a Yaris evolving into an MR2, as spotted by CarBuzz .

📌 The Core Development

It’s called the Yaris M concept, and it’s a further developed prototype of the car of the same name that Toyota showed off at last year's Tokyo Auto Salon. Formerly just a Yaris hatchback shell with a turbocharged four-cylinder engine where the rear seats should be, the new Yaris M features full-on coupe bodywork with massive rear flares.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

The silhouette isn't a complete surprise, as it’s a near match for Toyota’s 2027 WRC concept, which was spotted testing in Portugal this past spring. This Super Taikyu racer looks to be the tarmac version of that prototype.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

The engine isn’t the GR Yaris’ frenetic little three-banger, but a new four-cylinder called the G20. Displacing 2.0 liters, it's turbocharged up to around 400 to 450 horsepower and has already proved its mettle in endurance racing.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Everyone who owned a second-generation MR2 Turbo has permission to start jumping up and down excitedly because this new car looks like a return of that particular F355-on-a-budget machine. Note also that one of the four drivers who will be campaigning the car in Super Taikyu is none other than Akio Toyota, using his Morizo nom de guerre.

While a potential return of one of Toyota’s 1990s performance heroes is something to get excited about all on its own, the further development of this G20 turbo four is no less intriguing. A reliable powerplant putting out 200 horsepower per liter of displacement could have all kinds of applications, including in the rumored return of the Celica as a replacement for the GR Corolla.
